questions.q: Explain the different emphases of the First and Second Five Year Plans.
answer: After Independence, India chose planned development through the Planning Commission, and the first two Five Year Plans had very different emphases.

answer.text: The First Five Year Plan, from 1951 to 1956, gave priority to agriculture, irrigation and the rehabilitation of refugees from Partition. It was based on the Harrod-Domar model, which stressed raising savings and investment. Building large dams, which Nehru called the temples of modern India, was central to it. The aim was to lift the country out of food shortage and rural poverty.

The Second Five Year Plan, from 1956 to 1961, shifted the emphasis to rapid industrialisation, especially heavy and machine-making industries in the public sector. It was based on the Mahalanobis model, prepared by the statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, in the belief that heavy industry would make the country self-reliant and lay the base for future growth.

answer: Thus the First Plan focused on agriculture, while the Second Plan turned decisively towards industry.

questions.q: What development model did India adopt after Independence, and why?

answer.text: India adopted a model of planned development based on a mixed economy, seeking a middle path between capitalism and socialism.

list: The state took the lead in heavy industry and infrastructure, where private capital was weak
The private sector was allowed in other areas, under regulation

answer.text: It suited India's needs and values.

list: A poor, newly free country needed the state to build the base for growth and to promote equality
Planning through Five Year Plans aimed to use scarce resources wisely for growth with social justice

questions.q: What were the debates between the advocates of agriculture and of industry in India's early planning?

answer.text: saw a real debate over whether to give priority to agriculture or to heavy industry.

list: They held that India should first invest in agriculture and land reform to remove poverty and hunger
Only then, they said, could industry be built on a firm base

answer.text: This view prevailed in the Second Plan.

list: They believed heavy industry would make India self-reliant and lay the foundation for long-term growth
Critics feared this neglected agriculture and jobs — a tension that shaped later policy
